la:noun:sodalis.gloss: companion, mate, fellow, intimate, comrade, crony
senses: companion, mate, fellow, intimate, comrade, crony
member or fellow of an organisation; accomplice, conspirator
la:noun:sodalis.html:
sŏdālis, is (abl., regularly, sodali;
sodale,; ), comm.
cf. Sanscr. svadhā, will, power; Gr. ἔθος, custom; v.
.
In gen., a mate, fellow, intimate, comrade, crony, boon-companion, etc. (freq.and class.; a favorite word with Plautus; cf.: socius, familiaris): tuos amicus et sodalis,: hic sodalis tuos amicus optimus,; so (with amicus) : sodalem me esse scis gnato tuo,: sex sodales repperi, Vitam, amicitiam, etc.,: quid enim aut illo fidelius amico aut sodale jucundius?: si frater aut sodalis esset,: sodalis et familiarissimus Dolabellae, Lentul. ap. : primum habui semper sodales. Sodalitates autem me quaestore constitutae sunt sacris Idaeis ... epulabar igitur cum sodalibus omnino modice, etc. (shortly after: coetu amicorum),: popularis et sodalis,: meus sodalis,: adulescentes aliquot, aequales sodalesque: adulescentium Tarquiniorum,: in urbem reversus sodalibus legi,: Pompei meorum prime sodalium,: gaudentem parvisque sodalibus et lare certo Et ludis,: sodalis istius (Verris) in hoc morbo et cupiditate,: veterem tutare sodalem,: O jucunde sodalis,: dilectos inter sors prima sodalis,.—
In the poets, adject.: turba sodalis,the band of friends,.—Of things: Hebrus,: cratera,.—
In partic.
A fellow or member of a corporation, society, fraternity, college, etc.: sodales sunt, qui ejusdem collegii sunt, quam Graeci ἑταιρίαν vocant, .—Of the members of a college of priests: sodales in Lupercis,: Sodales Titii,: Augustales,; ; ; ; ; ; 1611 et saep.—
In a bad sense, a participator, accomplice in unlawful secret associations (esp. for buying votes, plotting against the State, etc.): quos tu si sodales vocas, officiosam amicitiam nomine inquinas criminoso,: tu in illis es decem sodalibus: Te in exsilium ire hinc oportet,.—
A gallant, ; .

senses: banquet-club (gathered to eat and dine together)
la:noun:sodalitas.html:
sŏdālĭtas, ātis, f.
sodalis
.
Lit., fellowship, companionship, brotherhood, friendship, intimacy; abstr. and concr. (class.; cf. societas): sodalitas familiaritasque,: summā nobilitate homo, cognatione, sodalitate, collegio,: intima sodalitas,.—Concr.: nunc ego de sodalitate solus sum orator datus,. —Plur.: aliquem a sodalitatibus abducere,.—
Transf.
A society, association of any kind, esp. for religious purposes (syn. sodalicium): fera quaedam sodalitas et plane pastoricia germanorum Lupercorum,: SODALITAS PVDICITIAE SERVANDAE,.—
A company assembled for feasting, a banqueting - club: sodalitates autem me quaestore constitutae sunt sacris Idaeis ... epulabar igitur cum sodalibus modice, etc.,.—
In a bad sense, an unlawful secret society: eodem die senatus consultum factum est, ut sodalitates decuriatique discederent, etc.,; .

la:adv:sodes.html:
sōdes
contr. from si audes, for audies, ; cf.: dic mihi si audes, quis ea est, etc., Plaut. Fragm. ap.
; in colloq. lang. (esp. freq. with an
imper.), if you will, if you please, with your leave, prithee, pray.
With imper.: dic sodes mihi, Bellan' videtur specie mulier?; so, dic sodes (mihi),; ; ; ; ; : emitte sodes, ne enices fame, sine ire pastum,: mitte ad

nos sodes Adelphasium tuam, : da sodes,; cf.: da mihi hoc sodes,: i sodes intro,: tace sodes,: jube sodes nummos curari,: vescere sodes,: corrige sodes,: sodes, dic,: inspice, sodes, et saep.: mane dum sodes,: vide etiam sodes,: aliud (vinum) lenius sodes vide,: aut sodes mihi redde decem sestertia, aut, etc.,.—

In other connections: at scin' quid, sodes?; : tene relinquam an rem. Me, sodes,: jam cedo tu sodes, qui occeperas, fabulam remetire,: o sodes, quoties tibi loquenti Byzantina sophos dedere regna,.
